volume.author: spec-author seat, group G5 Owner surface, round 1

contents.entry: Mechanism: Intake.Answer and the one-ruling rule
The four sources of an answer
How it starts without an agent typing
Every wait, its timeout and its fallback
State paths and their cleanup scripts

pointers.sibling: JSON schema of owner.answer and ruling
Bearings page service: the owner's answer leaves the page here
Controls screen: control.action enters as an owner action
Watcher: the second deliverer of every answer
Card builder: the ruling closes the card
Ticket intake: a ruling that unblocks a dead ticket
pointers.shared: Who may relay an owner answer
Where this node goes live in the one cut-over order of the book

purpose.is: The intake turns the owner's pick and words on a card into one ruling record in the store that every gate and cut-over node reads, with exactly one ruling per card id, whoever delivers it and however many times.
purpose.is-not: It never interprets the words, never decides for the owner, and never types anything into an agent.
purpose.why: Today an answer is a line in answers.jsonl read by one wait loop and typed into one pane (L08 finding 1); a relayed answer from chat (C42, "went recommended", recorded by hand) had no system path; and rulings that a gate checks were sometimes unrecorded (memory rulings-gates-check-are-records: PR 156 reworked). A ruling is a record or it did not happen.
purpose.decisions: D12 system lane (C40), D15 the owner holds the line through cards (C50), D10 one store (C34), no-bureaucracy-creep (an answer given where the owner is, recorded as the card's answer), rulings-gates-check-are-records.

record.field: a-<UTC compact>-<5 random>, generated by the page or the CLI, idempotent
the owner's own words, 4000 chars max (config max_words_chars)
owner for page; owner-cli plus the --session label for relay (shared/seat-contract.xml#relay); the policy id for policy; owner for controls
the tier the card was answered on

input.text: The record arrives by gRPC Intake.Answer from the page service (N-32) in the same request as the owner's tap, from the watcher (N-27) as the second deliverer, from the CLI coq owner answer --relay, from the standing policy at a deadline (N-28), or from the Controls screen (N-42) as a control.action wrapped as an answer to its own card. All five are the same record kind with a different source.

record.field: the card's cause record id, copied so gates can match on it without a join
UTC of the owner's act (not of the commit)
the re-entries the ruling triggers, as kinds: ticket.unblock, build-mode.set, gofactory, control.halt, control.resume, promotion.confirm, none

output.text: The ruling is immutable and keyed on the card id by idempotency key ruling:<card>; a second owner.answer for the same card yields answer.refused 409 with the existing ruling attached, and the page shows "already answered: <choice> at <at>" as an ack. The gates and cut-over nodes (N-44, N-49, N-50, N-03) subscribe to ruling records and read effects.

record.field: the card; the existing ruling id; shown to the owner as an ack
unknown card, pick out of range, card not open on this tier, words over cap, relay by a seat (COQ_SEAT set or a seat bundle; shared/seat-contract.xml#relay)

mechanism.where: Go service (D01), package internal/owner/intake, gRPC service Intake with one method Answer(AnswerRequest) returns (AnswerReply) on the control socket. The page service and the CLI are its only callers besides the watcher.
mechanism.step: Validate: the card record exists, is on the named tier, has no card.done; pick is within its options; words under the cap; source and by are consistent with the caller's identity on the socket (the page service may only send source=page or controls; the CLI under the owner's host CLI identity (owner uid, no COQ_SEAT, no seat bundle) may only send relay, and any CLI caller with a seat identity is refused; the builder may only send policy). A failure is answer.rejected 400, returned in the reply and written as a record so the page can show it and the health line can count it.

Persist the owner.answer record first (idempotent on its id: a repeat returns the stored record), so the owner's act is never lost even if the next step fails. This is V16's "persisted before acknowledged" carried into the store.

Rule: Store.Put the ruling with idempotency key ruling:<card> and expected version absent (create only). A 409 from the store means a ruling exists: return answer.refused 409 with that ruling. Otherwise the ruling is committed and the reply carries it.

Effects are computed by a rule table (tools/bearings/config/answer-effects.json, keyed on the card's template row and the pick): a pick that unblocks a dead ticket sets ticket.unblock with the ticket id (re-entry at N-03); a build-mode card sets build-mode.set with the expiry (N-44); the GOFACTORY card sets gofactory (N-49 and N-50); a control card sets control.halt or control.resume (shared/seat-contract.xml#halt-and-resume); a promotion confirm sets promotion.confirm naming the head sha, which N-09 reads before it merges a change to the owner-locked page assets (the one rule is nodes/N-48/spec.xml#owner-confirm). Nothing in this node acts on the effect; the subscribed node does, level-triggered, so a lost push never loses a ruling.
Close the card: N-28 writes card.done 200 on seeing the ruling; the intake does not write it (one writer per kind).

Ack: the reply to the page carries the ruling or the refusal; the page shows it as the answer's receipt (N-32 look). For a relay, the CLI prints the ruling id and the relayer's record is the ruling's by field (owner-cli plus the session label), not a separate note.
mechanism.text: Why the owner's at is the owner's act time: an answer relayed an hour later still rules at the time the owner spoke; gates compare rulings with records by cause, not by time, so the at field is for the owner's eye and the ledger.

Why words are never parsed: USERHALT and USERGO inside the words of an answer are not commands; commands are messages (N-30) or the Controls screen (N-42). A card about a halt has its options; the pick is the command.

sources-of-answers.source: The owner taps an option and types words on the bearings page (N-32); the page service calls Intake.Answer before it acks the browser; the watcher (N-27) delivers the same record a second time by stream and gets the same ruling back.

The owner answers in chat, on the phone, or in a terminal, and the owner, or the owner's own interactive architect session in the owner's terminal, runs coq owner answer --relay --card C-42 --pick 3 --words "owner answered in chat from the phone: went recommended" --session <label> under the owner's host CLI identity (shared/seat-contract.xml#relay). The by field is owner-cli plus the label; the record is a ruling with source=relay, and the page shows it on the card so the owner sees his own answer landed. A caller with COQ_SEAT set or a seat bundle (every dispatched role) is answer.rejected 400 reason relay-by-seat.

A standing policy row's deadline passes (N-28 step 3): the builder calls Intake.Answer with source=policy, by=<policy id>, pick=default; the ruling says so, and the page shows "defaulted by policy" on the closed card. The owner may overturn through the card the ruling re-opens if the template says it is overturnable (effects carry reopen).

An owner-initiated action on the Controls screen (N-42: hold, resume, build-mode, one-time break glass) is a card the screen itself posts and answers in one act; the ruling's source is controls so a later reader can tell a tap from a card answer. Break glass stays one time by the seat contract (a second break.glass ruling on one request id is answer.refused).

start.text: Intake is a gRPC service inside coq.service (N-06 unit.start); it is up when the service is up. It ships dark behind intake.enabled in the service config and goes live by its own ticket with the proof: one page answer on dev produces a ruling, a second answer on the same card is refused 409, a relayed answer on dev produces a ruling with source=relay. The old answers.jsonl path stays until the cut-over step in N-32's runbook migrates it.

wait.fallback: retry 3 times (200 ms apart); then answer.rejected 400 with reason store, which the page shows as 'not recorded, try again' and keeps the answer queued locally (N-32) for its own 3 retries
retry 3 times (1, 2, 4 s) then reply unavailable 503 to the caller; the page keeps the answer queued and retries; the watcher's stream delivery is the second path

retry 3 times; a 409 is success (the ruling exists); a timeout after 3 tries replies 503 and the owner.answer record stays with no ruling, which the tick (N-06) lists every second as answers-without-ruling and re-runs step 3 for, so no answer can be persisted and never ruled
keep the last good table; the ruling is written with effects=[] and a ruling.effects.unknown 500 alert so a reader does not act on a wrong effect; the tick re-computes effects when the table reloads

waits.no-cog: The cog that could stall this node is the store. Timeout: 3 tries. Fallback: the page's local queue, the watcher's second delivery and the tick's answers-without-ruling scan. No agent sits between the owner's tap and the ruling.

retries.rule: Every store call retries 3 times with backoff then reports with a 500 or 503 record; the answers-without-ruling scan on every tick is the recovery, and it is idempotent because the ruling key is the card id.
An answer is never dropped: it is persisted before anything else, and a persisted answer is ruled by the scan within one tick of the store returning.

many-agents-at-once.readers: Any number of seats read this volume; the effects table is one file edited by one ticket at a time.
many-agents-at-once.workers: Build tickets from this node touch internal/owner/intake, the Intake proto service, tools/bearings/config/answer-effects.json and the CLI verb coq owner answer; the page, the builder and the watcher own other files.

collision.what: the owner answers one card on two devices within the same second

many-agents-at-once.collision: Two owner.answer records persist (both are his acts); step 3 commits one ruling by create-only put; the second caller gets answer.refused 409 and its device shows already answered with the winning choice. Nothing is lost and nothing is double-applied.

collision.what: the page service and the watcher deliver the same owner.answer

many-agents-at-once.collision: Same record id: persist is a no-op, step 3 returns the existing ruling; both callers get the same reply.

collision.what: a relay races the owner's own page answer

many-agents-at-once.collision: First commit wins by card id; the loser is refused with the winner attached. The page shows which one landed; if they differ, the owner sees it on the card and may re-open through a new card. The relay CLI prints the refusal and the winner so the architect never records a wrong ruling.

collision.what: a policy default and the owner's answer at the deadline second

many-agents-at-once.collision: Same rule: one wins by create-only put. A policy ruling carries reopen so the owner's late answer becomes a new card, which is the "owner may overturn" rule of V17 kept honest.

collision.what: two coq.service instances during an upgrade

many-agents-at-once.collision: Both run the same code against one store; create-only puts and idempotent persists make every call safe to repeat on either.
many-agents-at-once.test: tests run two Intake clients firing the same and different answers to one card under the fake clock: exactly one ruling, every caller receives either the ruling or a 409 carrying it, the scan rules a persisted answer whose first put timed out.

permissions.runs-as: inside coq.service as the owner user; the Intake service is on the control socket, mode 0600
permissions.callers: page service (source page or controls), watcher (second delivery, any source as stored), card builder (source policy), the coq CLI under the owner's host CLI identity (source relay; shared/seat-contract.xml#relay)
permissions.may-not: a worker, reviewer or spec-author seat may never call Intake.Answer; a pod never reaches the socket (D23: no secret access, host-only socket)
permissions.identity: the caller's seat identity comes from the socket peer credentials and the seat bundle (N-13), never from a field in the request

op.name: an answer shows as not recorded on the page

runbook.op: the page retried 3 times and the store was down; check coq.service (N-06 runbook); the queued answer in the browser posts itself when the page reconnects; the watcher's stream delivery is the backstop
coq owner import-answers --file ~/.bearings/coq-stable/answers.jsonl --dry-run, then --yes; refuses if any id already exists unless --skip-existing

sources.source: N-29 re-entry: one ruling per card id; a second answer refused
finding 1: the consumer is an LLM seat typed into by herdr agent prompt
durable-then-acknowledge; accepted vs consumed vs completed
pick validated against the deck's options; words capped; appended to answers.jsonl
ANSWER line shape: id, decide, choice, words
a relayed answer recorded by hand: "owner answered in chat from the phone: went recommended"
post the ruling as a record before prompting; an unrecorded ruling cost PR 156 a rework
when a card cannot reach him, the question comes to him where he is and his answer is recorded as the card's answer
V16 idempotent ids; V17 deadline and default
break glass: owner-only and one time; the chosen option as a record on the asking ticket
answer field: the id of the request that is also the card id
machine verdict merges; owner holds via cards

item.reason: L08 finding 1; the consumer of a ruling is the store and the subscribed node, never a context window
K03 agents waiting by polling; tools/bearings/AGENTS.md already forbids it

item.what: parsing USERHALT or USERGO out of answer words
item.reason: commands are messages (N-30) or the Controls screen (N-42); a card's pick is its command

item.what: letting a later answer overwrite a ruling
item.reason: gates already read the first; an overwrite is a silent change of the past; a new card is the honest path

item.what: an answer record without a stored owner.answer (ruling only)
item.reason: the owner's act must persist before anything can fail
